items.title: 68252_Jay Cee
items.q: He also mentioned talks with Gene Buck of ASCAP

ctx.x: On April 24th, 1979, a day on which he was lying on bed, lying on the bed totally enervated, washed out, we began talking about music. And he was telling me how he never had to labor over his music. He said that a tune comes into his head and his fingers. Quote, "I can be lying here and a tune will hit me, and I can get up and go to the piano and play what was in my mind before and then elaborate on it. Just that easy, the tune wants out, and the best thing is to let it out."

He also mentioned talks with Gene Buck of ASCAP, et cetera, which I think referred to earlier in the tape. As to Irving Berlin, he said, "Ah, what a wonderful guy. There'll never be another like him. He's the one and only Irving Berlin. I'll never forget the first song he ever wrote, 'When I Lost You'" -- incidentally, we do have reference to this earlier on the tape.

He later mentioned George Whiting being one of the few names to work with Berlin, and they wrote a song, "My Wife's Going to the Country, Hooray, Hooray." I may have mentioned that earlier too. We talked about the turn of the century and the impact of the Wright Brothers.
